groups.title: Settle managed identity, sessions and sensitive-action authentication
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Settle managed identity, sessions and sensitive-action authentication.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-09 - Design verified account linking and protected owner actions
Use Cognito managed sign-in and explicit verified linking to an owner identity; never merge users from email equality alone. Keep browser cookie/CSRF and native PKCE/token storage designs separate. Bind a fresh step-up proof to a specific sensitive action and its proposed values, with expiry and server checks.
Owner decision: Resolve under MP-11: linking enrolment/recovery, step-up proof, devices, token revocation and two independent passkey recovery paths.

- Document sign-in/link/recovery/revoke sequences for Apple, Google and local passkey identities, including lost-device/account cases.
- Admin approvals bind owner, environment, action, payload hash and expiry; a generic logged-in session is insufficient.
- Cross-environment tokens, stale approval, CSRF, linking takeover and native redirect interception have negative cases.

### CT-01 - Define the owner-sensitive action and fresh-authentication policy
Keep the agreed Cognito managed sign-in. Propose recent server-verified authentication for record-affecting import confirmation, deletion, replay, credential linking/recovery, budget expansion and model promotion. Verify actual Cognito step-up availability and plan before deciding the mechanism; a local biometric unlock grants no server authority.
Owner decision: Owner approves the sensitive-action matrix, freshness window, assurance requirements and recovery fallback.

- Action matrix names read, propose, approve and execute permissions for every admin operation.
- Server checks owner, environment, session status, assurance and authentication age immediately before execution.
- Action challenge binds owner, environment, operation and exact target/payload hash; stale or reused proof fails.
- Tests include local-biometric-only, forged client claim, refreshed-old authentication, cross-environment proof and unavailable step-up capability.

### CT-17 - Specify personal identity linking, sessions and owner recovery
Design personal-owner recovery rather than household invites. Link only after verified control of both identities, use stable provider subjects rather than email equality and avoid unlinking the final usable path. Define web cookies/native secure storage and live-stream reauthorization.
Owner decision: Approve trusted origins/RP IDs, recovery inventory, session/stream revocation latency and loss-of-all-devices procedure.

- Email collision cannot merge identities or grant access; linking/recovery changes require current owner authorization.
- Revoked sessions cannot keep an SSE connection/data link indefinitely; explicit maximum delay is tested.
- A lost device can be revoked using an independent verified path without disabling the only owner irrecoverably.
- Dev/prod origin, issuer, audience, callback and passkey scope are explicit and fail on cross-environment tokens.

## Evidence and completion
- Record the exact decision, contracts, positive/negative/recovery acceptance and owner answer; remain open if unresolved.
- Link MP-19 reconciliation, phase/story map and planned Confluence pages. No claim that a proposal is accepted or implemented.
- Architecture and detailed phase/story baseline precede UX; full UX and separate owner permission precede build.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-01 - Remove conflicting current architecture authority
Make one versioned MP baseline the authority; preserve dated evidence as historical and replace conflicting current instructions. Add a decision precedence table and a source-to-phase-to-story crosswalk. Do not turn all ten layers into separately approved architectures.
Owner decision: Approve baseline structure, decision owner and handling of superseded ADRs.

- Every current instruction resolves to the same £100 all-in/direct Anthropic/DynamoDB-preferred direction.
- Every unselected option is marked open with an owner and deciding evidence.
- One current phase map has explicit historical epic crosswalk.

### CD-01 - Freeze the canonical MP baseline and detailed story trace
Keep PH identifiers, assign one current authority and explicitly supersede bootstrap conflicts. Decompose every relevant acceptance into MP contracts/tests and actual Jira stories before UX starts; retain MA provenance without copying dates or permissions.
Owner decision: Approve architecture baseline structure, epic crosswalk and story readiness protocol.

- Record versioned requirements, ADRs, contracts, phase/story links and source dispositions; no local draft ID is presented as Jira.
- All implementation stories have specific positive/negative acceptance, data/authority contracts, state inventory and dependency evidence before the UX gate.
- Architecture, complete UX and explicit build permission have separate owner approvals.

### CD-02 - Track rich-source limitations and MP visual evidence
Maintain a separate evidence state for source text, board semantics and actual visual inspection. Reuse MP native diagrams as proposed, update only for selected architecture and preserve exact versions/hashes. Create MP UX after baseline approval, not copied MA boards.
Owner decision: Approve required architecture/phase visual set and source-review boundaries.

- Every significant component and interface has a readable technical view with native AWS components and trust boundaries.
- Each visual records source, version, export hash and current/proposed status; reduced-motion/static alternatives retained.
- Uninspected referenced material remains visible as a limitation; no complete visual-parity claim.

### IR-01 - Decide whether usage-based UI personalisation belongs in MP
Default to static owner-configurable ordering until owner explicitly approves bounded personalisation; do not inherit autonomous reordering.

groups.title: Specify forecast tasks, scientific evaluation and model eligibility
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify forecast tasks, scientific evaluation and model eligibility.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### FC-02 - Define every forecast target and maturity contract
Define daily as-of origins for next-day, 5-20 trading-day and 3/6/12-calendar-month tasks. Specify terminal total return versus within-horizon drawdown as separate targets; 3-5-year outputs are conditional scenarios. Thirty-minute monitoring never creates a fresh formal forecast by implication.
Owner decision: Approve target catalogue, horizon list, origin cutoff, calendars, total-return convention and event thresholds.

- Each task pins target equation/unit, origin/cutoff, calendar roll, maturity, canonical source, baseline and metrics.
- Distinguish terminal loss from maximum drawdown, cost-basis loss and portfolio peak drawdown.
- Fixtures cover holidays, split/dividend, delayed NAV, FX and stale origins.

### FC-03 - Make historical datasets genuinely point in time
Require three times for observations (economic, known-at/publication, ingestion), revision lineage and versioned universe/exposures. Current adjusted prices, macro revisions, constituents and LLM extraction cannot be silently projected into past origins.
Owner decision: Approve first feature/data catalogue and classify sources as vintage-backed, lag-conservative, prospective-only or unavailable.

- Dataset manifest records source/query/cutoff/content hashes, actions and universe/exposure versions.
- Delisted/merged instruments and discontinued funds are addressed; missing history is explicit.
- Contaminated or reconstructable-only features excluded from claimed historical edge; prospective evidence separate.

### FC-04 - Specify a bounded experiment and leakage-control protocol
Choose rolling/expanding chronological origins with label-interval purging and training-only transformations. Group instruments by common time boundaries, account for serial/cross-asset dependence, record all trials and limit search. Final holdout is untouched until a frozen candidate comparison.
Owner decision: Approve fold schedule per horizon, search budget, selection loss, uncertainty method and final-test reuse policy.

- Leakage challenge cases fail for revised macro, future constituents, overlapping labels and extraction hindsight.
- All transforms/features/calibrators fit within permissible training data.
- Report paired baseline deltas, effective sample limits, subgroup performance and experiment count, not a best backtest alone.

### FC-05 - Fix the initial model catalogue without inventing model counts
Retain deterministic rules/statistical benchmarks and propose two CPU trainable families: regularised linear/logistic baselines and gradient-boosted/quantile challengers. Regime definitions and analog/event engines are explicit modules. Exact class/task/horizon artefacts follow evidence, not one model per ticker. SageMaker selection is separate infrastructure decision.
Owner decision: Approve candidate families, supported tasks, training cadence and bounded experiment count before final cost model.

- Catalogue separates rules, statistics, learned estimators, calibration and explanations.
- Each artefact has task/horizon/kind/eligible-universe/features/schema/dependencies/resource cap.
- Do not claim one trained object serves every market/horizon or that two families equal only two artefacts.

### FC-06 - Make analog and event evidence horizon-aware
Retain analog explanations but exclude candidates whose target outcome was not known at the origin; overlap/effective sample and distances must be visible. Event windows and confounding need predeclared definitions; eight events is not proof of an edge.
Owner decision: Approve analog feature/distance/window, weighting, de-overlap and sparse-evidence rules.

- Separate descriptive historical associations from causal claims.
- Report sample dates/count/effective dependence, similarity, outcomes/interval and coverage.
- Events known after the prediction origin cannot select the study cohort.

### FC-07 - Separate rule strength from calibrated forecast probability
Keep rule strength as a labelled heuristic until its event definition and calibration evidence are approved. Calibrators train on held-out chronological predictions; evaluate proper scores, reliability and interval coverage/width by horizon and important subgroup. No daily live recalibration without owner permission.
Owner decision: Approve calibration methods, loss functions, reliability bins/minimum evidence and rollback policy.

- No rule percentage silently displayed as P(up).
- Report Brier/log loss versus event base rates and range coverage plus sharpness; abstain where unsupported.
- Calibration version and approval bind every released forecast; model and calibrator cannot silently diverge.

### FC-08 - Design long-horizon investment inference independently of the four-week model
Use horizon-specific targets, data sufficiency and benchmarks. For long horizons consider simple valuation/fundamental/macro summaries only where licensed and truly known at time; compare against historical/constant-return and risk baselines. Scenarios use explicit contribution/return/inflation/FX assumptions, not fabricated confidence.
Owner decision: Approve scope/inputs/benchmarks for each long horizon and what may remain unavailable pending evidence.

- Keep all agreed horizons in requirements; do not replace them with20-day outputs.
- Display evaluated forecasts versus conditional scenarios with different labels and provenance.
- Account for few independent12-month outcomes and avoid claiming10years means thousands of independent yearly examples.

### FC-09 - Replace calendar-only practice gates with evidence and approval
Define task-specific shadow minimums using mature outcomes, effective independence, baseline deltas and confidence, plus owner promotion. Preapprove a narrow safety-disable route; distinguish data outage/model-ineligible from statistical deterioration.
Owner decision: Approve entry/promotion/monitoring/pause/rollback criteria and evidence minimums by horizon.

- Eight weeks cannot validate a12-month forecast.
- Promotion references immutable data/model/calibration/evaluation evidence and previous safe version.
- Safety disable preserves immutable forecasts and marks affected displays; return to live follows approved policy.

### FC-14 - Treat patterns as tested features rather than asserted alpha
Preserve pattern research concept but predefine detector, lag, confirmation, parameter grid and eligible kinds. Compare incremental effect against simple trend/risk baseline after multiple-testing controls and costs. NAV-only funds get only compatible line patterns.
Owner decision: Approve initial bounded pattern set and promotion/retirement evidence; wider catalogue remains planned.

- No look-ahead extrema or chart labelling using future bars.
- Hand-marked detector cases separate from out-of-sample value tests.
- Source-adjustment/corporate-action artefacts and thin trading do not create fake pattern signals.

### FC-15 - Validate each market and instrument family before extension
Make exchange/session/calendar, corporate-action/unit/price semantics, entitlements, historical universe and test evidence explicit capabilities. India is part of initial requirements rather than a copied final phase. Each future market/theme/model follows approved extension checklist with separate source/cost validity.
Owner decision: Approve v1 supported kinds, India NAV scope, exchange calendars and per-market readiness tests; defer unsupported families explicitly.

- US/UK/India each has source/identity/FX/action/calendar/forecast evidence examples.
- GBX versus GBP, NSE/BSE linkage, accumulation/distribution and direct/regular mutual-fund plans are distinct.
- Future China/Taiwan/HK/Europe configuration cannot bypass rights or scientific gates.

### FC-16 - Fix the forecast information contract before drawing screens
Agree content/state and provenance contracts before UX. Preserve forecast/proof/track record plus disagreement, stale, insufficient history, no-clear-view, disabled, corrected-outcome and cost-paused states. Actual layout/style/options come later.
Owner decision: Approve information hierarchy, action labels and required proof/state payloads; do not approve MA branding or mock values.

- Each displayed number identifies task/as-of/source/model and whether evaluated, illustrative or scenario.
- Proof contains dataset/fold/baseline/mature outcomes/eligibility and limitations, with accessible text alternatives.
- Chat deep-links exact evidence context; offline/stale data cannot masquerade as fresh analysis.

## Evidence and completion
- Record the exact decision, contracts, positive/negative/recovery acceptance and owner answer; remain open if unresolved.
- Link MP-19 reconciliation, phase/story map and planned Confluence pages. No claim that a proposal is accepted or implemented.
- Architecture and detailed phase/story baseline precede UX; full UX and separate owner permission precede build.

groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify performance, exposure and ranked investment decisions.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### FC-10 - Close realised-performance and benchmark accounting decisions
Reuse MP ledger boundary decisions; define portfolio/account/holding XIRR separately and benchmark contributions with matched dates/currencies. Retained dividends, reinvestment and transfers are not duplicate external flows. Add time-weighted comparison only when valuation evidence supports it; no extrapolated missing history.
Owner decision: Approve rounding/residual tolerances, FX timing, terminal valuation, root ambiguity, benchmark and supported performance methods.

- Golden cases include same-day, missing history, multiple roots, internal transfer, fees/dividends and FX.
- Reconcile booked cash/cost basis separately from quote-adjusted total-return series.
- State unavailable per metric and preserve working/provenance; XIRR never serves as predictive probability.

### FC-11 - Specify portfolio exposure and risk without false precision
Define portfolio snapshots, weight basis, partial coverage, cash and cross-listed exposure before ranking. Separate instrument trading currency from underlying economic exposure and hedging. Estimate correlations/covariance on aligned eligible data with declared shrinkage/missingness and stress alternatives.
Owner decision: Approve exposure completeness thresholds, risk windows and benchmark/weight conventions.

- Double-listed securities and fund overlap do not double-count underlying economic risk.
- Coverage residual and source age visible; absent exposure is not zero.
- Show investment versus FX return effects and use partial-data abstention for unsupported portfolio-risk estimates.

### FC-12 - Make ranked actions a deterministic versioned decision policy
Define component eligibility/scaling and action semantics before combining scores. Growth/risk/benchmark evidence must be comparable or explicitly unavailable. Distinguish forecast probability, preference-weighted ranking and portfolio constraint; explain conflicts and ask owner for any change.
Owner decision: Approve score normalisation, abstention/conflict policy, concentration/contribution constraints and recommendation wording.

- Show component scores/weights/source/version and counterfactual portfolio impact.
- Missing component does not silently earn neutral/full score; disclose approved renormalisation policy.
- No trade execution, universal sell-everything instruction, tax-rule assumptions or autonomous contribution changes.

groups.title: Choose durable workflows and define API queue replay semantics
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Choose durable workflows and define API queue replay semantics.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-04 - Specify the authenticated SSE delivery contract and operating budget
Keep short commands/queries and durable jobs separate from observation. Recommend Regional REST API streaming with explicit Python Web Adapter compatibility, bounded stream lifetime, per-device/tab connection caps and event IDs. Replace the MA 200ms/1-second polling targets with a measured latency/cost envelope suited to personal use.
Owner decision: Approve replay retention, latency target, auth/session approach, refresh/reconnect and polling cadence.

- Specify handshake/auth, event schema, ordering, after-cursor, heartbeat, resync and logout/revocation behaviour.
- Disconnect does not cancel an accepted job or trigger duplicate provider calls.
- Cost scenario counts active device hours, Lambda GB-seconds, DynamoDB reads and reconnect bursts; no all-day stream assumed free.

### PL-05 - Define queue, outbox, replay and external-side-effect semantics
Use stable business IDs, durable claims/leases and an atomic application outbox. Standard SQS for independent work; FIFO only for ordering that is actually required, such as a conversation. Distinguish scheduler target failures from worker failures; quarantine permanent invalid inputs without infinite retries.
Owner decision: Approve queue topology, ordering partitions, retention/replay authority and ambiguous-provider-call reconciliation.

- Message table defines producer/consumer, schema, key, ordering, lease, visibility, max attempts, concurrency and failure destination.
- Crash cases span before/after provider submission, database commit, outbox dispatch and acknowledgement; ambiguous paid calls are not blindly resubmitted.
- Partial batch failure/FIFO order and stale or expired owner approvals have explicit cases.

### PL-06 - Choose one orchestration mechanism for cross-service jobs
Recommend Step Functions Standard for the proposed cross-service SageMaker/import/approval workflows because visual state and native service joins match the requested technical/admin evidence. Compare Lambda Durable Functions as the code-first alternative rather than adding both by default. State-machine payloads should carry opaque references, not private documents or credentials.
Owner decision: Owner selects Step Functions versus Durable Functions after a representative failure/retry/wait/cost comparison.

- One representative import and train-evaluate-approve journey is specified in both alternatives with equivalent guarantees.
- Runtime/container/SDK/region evidence is explicit: managed durable Python3.13/3.14 are listed, while OCI images support additional versions; Python3.12 is not declared impossible.
- Replay/timeout/cancellation state retention and sensitive-payload redaction are documented.

### CT-14 - Bound self-healing, replay and recovery authority
Automatically retry only explicitly idempotent work within approved bounds. New external calls, financial reprocessing, broad replay, deleting evidence or increasing spend require current policy/approval. Use isolated restore plus reconciliation before switching authority.
Owner decision: Approve incident classes, automatic recovery allowlist, replay limits, RPO/RTO and operator escalation path.

- Replay preserves original business id and generates new attempt/trace links; duplicates cannot double-commit or double-notify.
- Replays recheck current owner permissions, source retention/deletion and latest applicable config.
- Restore exercise proves ledger/audit/source/model joins and deletion tombstones, not just object availability.
- No app agent can grant infrastructure permissions or perform an unapproved production apply.

## Evidence and completion
- Record the exact decision, contracts, positive/negative/recovery acceptance and owner answer; remain open if unresolved.
- Link MP-19 reconciliation, phase/story map and planned Confluence pages. No claim that a proposal is accepted or implemented.
- Architecture and detailed phase/story baseline precede UX; full UX and separate owner permission precede build.

Daily scheduled inference can run once per eligible universe/horizon then serve stored results. - Serving estimates compare stored daily results/Lambda, Batch Transform and Serverless with loading/cold-start/egress/storage included.
- Serverless exclusions are explicit: no VPC configuration, network isolation, data capture or Model Monitor; private-training controls do not automatically transfer.

groups.title: Specify bounded Anthropic research tools batches and memory
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify bounded Anthropic research tools batches and memory.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-02 - Settle agent roles, SDK loop and memory authority
Retain one controlled Anthropic client runner; specify deterministic work separately from Claude routes, with role/tool/context/budget/eval contracts. Keep Haiku/Sonnet classes as candidates and pin evaluated IDs later. Memory notes must have source, expiry, taint and correction/deletion semantics and may never replace ledger facts or approved settings.
Owner decision: Approve role-to-route catalogue, memory authority and per-route tool/budget limits; no automatic Opus route.

- A table enumerates each responsibility, trigger, compute unit, model-if-any, tools, outputs and forbidden operations.
- Ask/approve exits Lambda and resumes from a typed pending action rather than waiting for the owner.
- Model/prompt/tool/memory-version changes identify affected safety suites and require appropriate approval.

### PL-03 - Separate batch deadlines from live work and justify caching
Use batch only for nonurgent enrichment and bounded evals. Deadline-aware submission/polling and per-item state prevent delayed results from rewriting already-issued evidence. Cache eligible stable prefixes only when expected reuse pays its write premium; no artificial warming or guaranteed hit-rate assumption.
Owner decision: Approve batch-eligible workloads, freshness cutoffs, late-result policy and per-route cache policy.

- Pending batch liability is reserved once and reconciled by item/custom ID; unordered, expired and partial results have cases.
- The briefing uses last-valid dated evidence, deterministic prose or pending labels when the batch misses its cutoff.
- Cold-cache, no-cache, best-effort batch-hit and per-model-version cost cases are costed.

### FC-13 - Evaluate LLM-derived news factors separately from narrative quality
Freeze extraction schema/entity links/source rights, publication/extraction times and model/prompt versions. Test extraction accuracy and downstream incremental predictive value separately. Historical extraction by a newer LLM is potentially hindsight-contaminated; prospective shadow is the default when contamination cannot be bounded.
Owner decision: Approve factor catalogue, labelled extraction sample, provenance requirements, relevance floor and ablation criteria.

- No live-risk dependency on a batch not guaranteed complete by deadline.
- Every financial number and relevance weight computed from authorised typed inputs.
- LLM judge cannot manufacture price ground truth or override promotion/admission controls.

### CT-07 - Freeze a typed agent/tool capability manifest
Declare roles independently from LLM routes. Runtime policy checks tool, owner/environment scope, schema/ranges, side effect, current approval, repetition, remaining time/cost and untrusted-content state. Fail closed when policy is unavailable.
Owner decision: Approve the v1 roles/tools, permitted read/draft actions, external research surface and numerical-service ownership.

- No model prompt or agent message can grant a new tool, secret access, trade capability, budget or promotion authority.
- Each entry maps to at least one negative safety case and useful capability/regression case.
- Policy applies to every application-side tool invocation and rechecks permission before committing.
- Provider-hosted tools are constrained at request admission because application middleware cannot intercept every internal action.

### CT-08 - Define quarantine and public/private research boundaries
Treat PDFs, screenshots, merchant/issuer text, web results and agent notes as untrusted data. Use no-tool structured extraction and validate fields/provenance; keep public research requests free of holdings quantities/private documents. Carry taint through summaries and memory. Test residual misinformation even when exfiltration is blocked.
Owner decision: Approve minimum outbound context by route, whether any optional classifier is justified and what happens when evidence is suspicious.

- Poisoned PDF/image/OCR/news/tool-result cases cannot cause a prohibited tool, disclosure or record mutation.
- Structured output does not automatically count as truthful; schema validity, source references and field plausibility are checked separately.
- Outbound tool URLs/arguments are policy-controlled and sensitive context cannot enter public web research.
- A screening refusal, timeout or no verdict is not an allow decision; safe extraction/abstention remains available.

### CT-09 - Specify numerical and evidence grounding by claim type
Ground rendered financial claims in typed tools and exact snapshot/as-of/version references. Verify amount, currency/unit, sign, horizon and uncertainty label; matching a number somewhere in context is insufficient. Scientific probabilities and scenarios have separate eligibility checks.
Owner decision: Approve allowed financial claim types, numeric tolerances, citation freshness and safe failure/fallback experience.

- Contradicted/stale values, wrong currency/unit, invented probability and swapped horizons fail even when the number exists in another tool output.
- Figures derived from multiple values are calculated by deterministic services with formula versions.
- Every recommendation can open its exact evidence context without a new unsupported reconstruction.
- Failed grounding abstains or uses an approved deterministic template within the budget; retries are bounded.

### CT-15 - Separate learning proposals, approved settings and memory
Use read-only defaults; propose rather than mutate model/prompt/rule/budget settings. Distinguish evaluated numerical calibration, research notes and user preferences. Memory is sourced/tainted/revisable and cannot become ledger truth or authority.
Owner decision: Approve any automatic safe adjustments, owner promotion scope, memory classes, forgetting and poisoning controls.

- Every proposed model/rule/prompt change pins mature outcome evidence and relevant safety/eval/cost impact.
- A note or summary cannot overwrite source data, outcomes, thresholds or an approved configuration.
- Drift or insufficient mature evidence triggers abstention/shadow/disable according to policy, never autonomous promotion.
- Version rollback preserves original forecast and outcome history.

## Evidence and completion
- Record the exact decision, contracts, positive/negative/recovery acceptance and owner answer; remain open if unresolved.
- Link MP-19 reconciliation, phase/story map and planned Confluence pages. No claim that a proposal is accepted or implemented.
- Architecture and detailed phase/story baseline precede UX; full UX and separate owner permission precede build.

groups.title: Specify offline online and human-calibrated agent evaluations
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify offline online and human-calibrated agent evaluations.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### CT-10 - Define MP T0/T1/T2 with coverage and incomplete outcomes
Propose T0 offline deterministic replays on relevant changes; T1 bounded live tests for affected agent/tool/prompt/SDK routes; T2 full affected qualification for model/routing/release changes. Select case/trial counts from failure risk and budget rather than copying MA3/5 trials or dollar caps. Keep ML temporal validation separate.
Owner decision: Approve harness, v1 case inventory, coverage triggers, per-run/month limits and which unresolved failures block a release.

- Case metadata links requirement, phase/story, agent/tool, threat or capability, fixture version and expected state invariants.
- A changed tool without mapped tests blocks readiness; unsupported dynamic plug-ins cannot bypass coverage.
- Budget exhaustion, missing model access, timeout and invalid fixtures report incomplete/error rather than pass.
- Original answer outputs and appended scorer versions remain auditable, and no live API is called by ordinary unit tests.

### CT-11 - Calibrate judges using independent labels and uncertainty
Use a separate binary/ordinal rubric per failure mode plus unknown, independent held-out owner labels and confidence intervals for false positives/negatives. Report strata such as extraction, research, financial explanation and market. Remain advisory while evidence is insufficient.
Owner decision: Approve severity-specific error tolerance, sampling mix, recalibration cadence and sufficient evidence; MA50pass/50fail and0.8 are reference values only.

- Judge calibration labels are separate from judge prompt development and repeat examples cannot inflate sample count.
- Low sample size or a changed judge/model/rubric resets eligibility or triggers requalification.
- Sample both suspicious and apparently successful runs, record selection probabilities and avoid presenting oversampled-failure rates as population rates.
- Judge disagreement routes to owner review; an LLM judge cannot certify numerical truth or model predictive performance.

### CT-12 - Resolve evaluation privacy and batch-result evidence
Start with synthetic/redacted fixtures. Actual portfolio transcripts need a separately documented minimum payload and provider feature/retention assessment. Asynchronous judging is nonurgent, item-versioned and reconciled; archive only necessary protected evidence, not indiscriminate full prompts.
Owner decision: Approve real-data evaluation eligibility, provider batch use, transcript/label retention and deletion semantics.

- Register which data leaves AWS for each model API feature, purpose and account arrangement.
- Partial/expired/cancelled batch items stay distinct from successful judge coverage and retain original run references.
- Late results cannot overwrite newer adjudication, labels or decisions.
- Synthetic regression cases preserve failure shape without retaining real account details; owner confirms release to the case corpus.

groups.title: Specify run evidence telemetry and conservative cost admission
groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify run evidence telemetry and conservative cost admission.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-12 - Specify trace joins and telemetry budgets without universal trace claims
Use durable business records as operational truth, with sampled OTel traces and explicit asynchronous links. A user action, a queue batch, a resumed approval and a stream session do not have to form one infinitely long parent-child trace. External provider internals are not observable solely because the SDK call is traced.
Owner decision: Approve telemetry backend/sampling/redaction and per-env cost envelope, coordinated with admin/audit lane.

- Define business/run/request/trace/span/message/provider IDs, propagation headers/attributes and link rules at every boundary.
- Test redaction, context injection/forgery, sampled-out requests and multi-message batches; Activity remains complete when a span is absent.
- Estimate dimensions, ingestion/query/retention/custom metrics/alarms rather than copying MA free-tier/£2.50 claims or assuming100% tracing.

### PL-13 - Make cost admission conservative across concurrent work and shared credits
Reserve conservative maximum liability before paid submissions, track unknown/retrying/batch commitments and reconcile once. Keep gross, verified credit and cash separate, shared credit counted once across apps. Dashboard reads cached aggregates; bill reports remain delayed even if polled six-hourly/daily.
Owner decision: Approve per-feature ceilings, staleness policy, allowed degradation and how shared/unknown credits affect admission.

- Concurrent final-pence requests cannot each independently pass the same remaining budget.
- Unknown credit/report availability refuses uncovered work; deterministic output remains available without silently upgrading paid routes.
- Include source subscription, FX/tax assumptions, telemetry, builds, training, backups and collectors in baseline and stress recosts; no guarantee AWS billing instantly stops.

### CT-05 - Specify run lifecycle evidence that survives crashes
Create accepted/started and terminal lifecycle evidence or equivalent durable job state, plus timeout reconciliation. Run summaries are not the only source for durable forecast and approval truth.
Owner decision: Approve timeout/stuck-run thresholds, the run summary schema and protected content-versus-metadata policy.

- Accepted jobs and started runs remain discoverable if a worker crashes before writing completion.
- A reconciler distinguishes missing, timed_out, cancelled, partial and ambiguous_external_outcome.
- Activity links the exact config/model/source versions, guard decisions, attempts and cost reservation.
- Completion is never inferred solely from a successful queue acknowledgement or stream close.

### CT-06 - Validate asynchronous trace joins and budgeted telemetry
Use stable business IDs as the durable join; adopt parent/child spans or span links according to asynchronous lifecycle and replay. Pin OTel convention/version and test every integration. Budget sampling, cardinality, queries and retention separately.
Owner decision: Choose the minimum launch signal set, trace sampling strategy, correlation fields and measured observability allowance.

- A synthetic UI→API→queue→worker→Anthropic/batch→storage→push example resolves through protected business IDs even after traces expire.
- Replay gets a new attempt/run and linked trace, not the original successful span rewritten.
- Trace headers are validated; client-provided baggage cannot inject identities, secrets or unbounded attributes.
- Leak tests cover raw prompts, holdings amounts, filenames, signed URLs, account identifiers and model/tool arguments.

### CT-13 - Specify conservative cost admission and billing reconciliation
Preserve confirmed£100all-in,£70operation+£30reserve and£60/75/85cash thresholds. Allocate evals, monitors, retries, cache writes and batches within the same envelope. Reserve before external work, carry ambiguous liabilities and distinguish pre-credit reported cost from cash/verified credit.
Owner decision: Approve feature/environment/eval suballocations, stale/unknown-credit thresholds and emergency minimum functions; resolve conflicting root rules.

- Shared credits are counted once and cannot be assumed available to MP merely because the account has promotional entitlement.
- Two concurrent requests cannot each spend the same remaining allowance.
- Dashboard uses cached reports with source age and reconciliation status; polling cadence is not guaranteed provider freshness.
- Permission/budget failure sends no uncovered request and does not silently switch to paid fallback.

- Link MP-19 reconciliation, phase/story map and planned Confluence pages. No claim that a proposal is accepted or implemented.
- Architecture and detailed phase/story baseline precede UX; full UX and separate owner permission precede build.

groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify owner admin approvals audit and launch controls.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### CT-02 - Specify the approval and configuration-change state machine
Use draft → validated → awaiting_owner → approved → executing → succeeded/failed/reconcile_required. Rejected, expired or cancelled proposals terminate without execution. Pin the exact proposal and expected prior config/ledger version; separate viewing a card, approving it and completing the operation.
Owner decision: Approve proposal expiry, allowed bounded automatic adjustments, rollback policy and which operations require a second confirmation.

- Approval evidence includes actor, target environment, prior/new version, payload hash, reason, affected forecasts, cost estimate and rollback plan.
- Changed inputs or stale prior version invalidate approval and require a new proposal.
- Concurrent approve/reject and duplicate execution produce at most one effective state transition.
- An approval failure or timeout leaves no silent partial financial/config update.

### CT-03 - Define durable business audit contracts and integrity claims
Separate durable financial/approval/source audit from expiring operational logs. Define atomic ledger/audit/outbox boundaries and detect missing/altered events. An append-only API is not by itself tamper-proof against privileged administrators.
Owner decision: Approve required audit record classes, privileged threat model, integrity-check mechanism and evidence retention.

- Every committed change links event/revision, original hash/version, actor, reason, confirmation and prior/superseding revision.
- Injected failure between financial commit, audit and outbox cannot leave an unreported inconsistency.
- Integrity exercises detect a removed or altered event and report coverage; gaps are not certified intact.
- Source access, denied actions and administrative changes have appropriate privacy-safe evidence.

### CT-16 - Define admin information architecture and launch-minimum controls before UX
Prepare an MP admin domain map covering Files/Imports, Audit, Runs/Health, Agents/Models/Evals, Approvals/Config, Costs/Budgets, Incidents/Recovery, Identity/Devices. Keep owner-only personal scope; do not import household-member administration or copy MA board styling.
Owner decision: Approve launch-minimum versus later depth, navigation/domain boundaries and action permissions before screen design.

- Every launch-sensitive action has a defined path, observable pending/failure/cancel/rejected state and evidence drill-down.
- Read-only cost/audit access is distinct from controls that change budgets, data or model state.
- Mobile and web workflows share backend contracts but have separately specified recovery/privacy/accessibility states.
- Phase pages cite actual MP stories/contracts and clearly distinguish planned UI from implemented functionality.

groups.description:
Planning outcome: Specify client compatibility release regression and alert delivery.

Research and specification only. MA concepts are reference; current MP owner decisions control. No application/infrastructure implementation, paid calls or automatic promotion.

## Decisions and acceptance

### PL-11 - Define MP release evidence and security regression layers
Carry the gates and immutable-promotion concepts, not MA tool/version counts or automatic dev-apply permission. Recommend one IaC stack family, OIDC per environment, pinned builds/SBOM and artifact provenance; local/stub replay tests offline by default, paid evals separately capped and approved.
Owner decision: Approve build/test/release matrix, IaC choice, vulnerability policy, browser/device service choice and Mac CI budget.

- Matrix links changes to unit/contract/integration/numeric/security/agent/web/native checks and identifies which are offline versus paid.
- One tested artifact is promoted with explicit prod approval and rollback evidence; source/data/schema/config changes have compatibility plans.
- Scanner findings have severity/exploitability/exception expiry ownership; incomplete or budget-exhausted evals never become green.

### PL-14 - Fix web/native ownership and offline/privacy contracts before UX
Recommend static SvelteKit PWA shell on S3/CloudFront with authenticated API data; add SSR only for a demonstrated need. Honour MP Swift ownership of native surfaces/cache/secure-device integration while RN owns navigation/bridge contracts. Define privacy-safe offline scope and durable reconnect independently for each platform.
Owner decision: Approve supported OS/devices (including what Duo means), cache/offline/push capabilities, bridge ownership and exact compatible stack; defer visual design until these contracts are settled.

- S3 static output does not imply SvelteKit server sessions/actions exist; session architecture is explicit.
- Offline owner/data clearance, logout, expiry, stale results and app/service-worker update cases are specified.
- Web and native have separate implementation stories using shared API/event contracts, not claims that one UI codebase is shared; widgets/Siri/share-sheet/LiveActivities are individually phased.

### CT-18 - Separate material investment alerts from operational incident routing
Maintain separate financial-risk, system-security, data-quality, billing and job-failure alert classes with correlation/dedup, explicit evidence and recovery state. Product push channels remain native/PWA plus app/chat; additional operator email is a choice.
Owner decision: Approve material/critical conditions, quiet-hour exceptions, grouping/cooldowns, emergency channel and weekend briefing.

- A downstream outage produces one incident with linked symptoms rather than one push per failed component.
- Risk alerts use eligible as-of data; unavailable providers cannot generate a confident all-clear.
- Push provider acceptance is labelled delivery attempt/acceptance, not proof the owner read it.
- Alert policy edits are versioned/audited; recovery notifications link the incident and do not erase prior failures.
